title: Link
description: Everything the phone and the Mac say to each other (openspec/specs/mac-link). Every request carries the Fantasia-Contract header with the contract version; every response carries a trace id. Unions are flat objects with a kind field, so the Kotlin side stays plain data classes.

message.description: Why, in words the player can read.

PairingInvite.description: What the Mac's pairing QR code holds.

code.description: One-time pairing code, valid for ten minutes.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the Mac's certificate, which the phone pins.

standing.description: Where the Story stands on its current Path, as one line: "Scene 14 · After curfew" mid-Scene, "Sunday 7:40 am · choosing where to go" at the Day View.

detail.description: The line under the standing: "Friday 9:52 pm · with Hermione" mid-Scene, "3 Scenes played" at the Day View.

at_label.description: Story time as people say it: "Friday 9:40 pm".

people.description: Who is in the Scene now besides the Player Character, with their Portraits; someone a Move or the Story brings in is added.

Passage.description: One Move or Reply, as it stands on the tree.

Exchange.description: A Move and the Reply that answered it. The opening Scene's first Reply has no Move.

TurnState.description: Whether a Reply is being written, has failed, or nothing is under way.

text_so_far.description: While writing: the Reply's words so far.

reason.description: When failed: why, in words the player can read.

trace_id.description: When writing or failed: the turn's trace id.

job.description: When failed: the job that failed.

SceneView.description: The Scene screen as the Mac sees it on the Story's current Path.

seq.description: The newest entry in the Story when this view was taken.

head_entry_id.description: The entry a Move must follow.

player_character.description: The name of the person the player plays, for labelling their Moves.

last_event_id.description: The id of the newest event this view reflects, including the words of a Reply under way; the live stream resumes after it.

focus.description: Who the Scene is focused on, or null.

day_view.description: Present once the Scene has closed, by the Story or by End scene: the Day View, whose composer takes the next Move.

previously.description: Present when the player last played this Story more than a day ago and the Scene they are in, or the Scene that closed at the Day View, has a summary: the Previously card.

opening.description: Present while a Move at the Day View is opening the next Scene and the Scene has not opened yet (openspec presence: Between Scenes is quiet, and shows progress). Then there is no Day View, the exchanges are that Move's, the Scene that closed is among the earlier Scenes, and the phone shows this card in place of the Scene's.

NextScene.description: The next Scene, being written: when it is, when the choice set a time.

at.description: Story time, "Day N HH:MM", or null when the choice set none.

at_label.description: As people say it: "Friday 6:00 pm", or null.

summary.description: The Chronicler's one line for the Scene, or empty until it has written one.

Previously.description: The Previously card: where the Story stands, from the Chronicler's records, and when the player last played.

summary.description: The latest summary of the Scene the player is in (so far), or of the Scene that closed.

since.description: When the player last played: the time the Path's head entry was written, ISO 8601.

after.description: The entry the phone saw as the head; a Move after any other is refused as stale.

StoryEvent.description: One event on a Story's live stream. Entry events (scene_opened, move, reply, scene_closed, focus_set, linger_set, redo, world_moved) are replayed after a reconnect; reply_started, reply_delta and reply_failed describe the turn under way; scene_end_step says which step of a Scene's end is under way, null when it is done, and scene_end_failed where it stopped and why (docs/adr/0016). path_changed says the Story is now on another Path, or its Path was moved back, or a Move or Reply on it was edited. After scene_opened, scene_closed, redo, world_moved, scene_end_step, scene_end_failed and path_changed, and after a move that opens the next Scene, the phone reads the Scene again, because they change more than one part of it.

seq.description: The newest entry this event follows.

scene.description: scene_opened and reply: the Scene's card as it stands.

text.description: reply_delta: the words that just arrived.

focus.description: scene_opened and focus_set: who the Scene is focused on, or null.

opening.description: move: present when the Move is written at the Day View, the next Scene it opens. The Scene is then that Move's, under this card, until scene_opened.

step.description: For scene_end_step and scene_end_failed: the step; null when the Scene's end is done.

DayView.description: Where and when the Player Character is between Scenes, and what he learned meanwhile (openspec day-view).

at_label.description: Story time as people say it: "Sunday 7:40 am".

day.description: The day as people say it: "Sunday", or "Day 3" when the Story has no weekdays.

time.description: The time as people say it: "7:40 am".

closed_by.description: Who closed the last Scene: the Story, whose closing Reply can be redone, or the player, with End scene.

scene_span.description: When the Scene that ended ran, as people say it: "Friday 9:40 pm – 11:05 pm".

meanwhile.description: What the Player Character learned while elsewhere, once the World has moved on; empty before.

happenings.description: What is on today that the Player Character could go to: at most four, the Story's pick first, once the World has moved on; empty before.

reaction.description: The player's reaction to the Scene that ended, or null.

when.description: How long to go: "3 days", "Tomorrow", "Today at 8:30 pm".

label.description: "3 days to Draconia's flying test", "Tomorrow: the first match", "Today at 6:00 pm: the feast".

MeanwhileItem.description: One line of Meanwhile, marked by how the Player Character learned it.

Happening.description: Something going on in the World at a time and place the Player Character could be at (openspec day-view: Up to four Happenings).

time.description: When, as people say it: "9:00 am", or "Tomorrow 9:00 am".

what.description: What is going on, and why it matters now.

who.description: Who will be there, by name.

expected.description: The Player Character is expected there: shown "You're expected".

pick.description: The Story's own pick, which Let the Story choose goes to.

days_away.description: How many days off it is: 0 today, 1 tomorrow; the Day View says "in 5 days" beyond that.

scene.description: The Stretch's Scene that matters it is, when it is one; null otherwise.

every.description: For a weekly Engagement, the day it repeats ("Wednesday"), and time is then the hour alone: shown "Every Wednesday · 7:30 pm". Null otherwise.

DayChoices.description: What the Day View's other choices offer: people to follow, places to go, and times to skip to.

follow.description: People the Player Character could follow: the Leads and whoever was in the Scene that ended.

places.description: The Story's places to go to.

Skip.description: A later time to skip to: this evening, tomorrow, the weekend, the next Landmark.

label.description: "This evening", "Tomorrow", "The weekend", or the Landmark's name.

in_sentence.description: The label as it reads inside a sentence: "this evening", "tomorrow", "the weekend", or the Landmark's name as named.

time.description: As people say it: "6:00 pm" on the Day View's own day, "Saturday 7:30 am" on another.

days_away.description: How many days off it is: 0 today, 1 tomorrow; the skip says "in 48 days" a week or more away.

ChooseRequest.description: A choice at the Day View (openspec day-view: The player chooses where to be). The Mac writes it as the player's Move, the Gap first.

after.description: The entry the choice follows: the Day View's head.

happening.description: go: the Happening's id; left out or null for the other kinds.

who.description: follow: who; left out or null for the other kinds.

place.description: somewhere: the place; left out or null for the other kinds.

at.description: skip: the time skipped to; left out or null for the other kinds.

gap.description: What the Player Character did in the Gap, in the player's words, or null: left blank, he spent it quietly where he was.

PathsView.description: The Paths screen (openspec paths: The Paths screen): the Story as a tree, laid out by the Mac in reading order.

clearable.description: How many Paths Clear would remove: those Rewind set aside and the player never opened.

PathRow.description: One row of the tree: a run of Scenes the Paths below share, folded; the Scene where they part; or a Path's card. Depth says how far in it is drawn.

label.description: scenes: "Scenes 1 – 12 · Friday 6:10 pm"; fork: "Scene 13 · Friday 8:05 pm"; path: its card's label.

title.description: fork: the Scene's title, "The troll"; otherwise null.

PathCard.description: A Path on the Paths screen.

label.description: "MAIN · YOU ARE HERE", "FROM SCENE 13 · TRIED ANOTHER WAY", "SET ASIDE AT SCENE 14", "FROM THE BEGINNING".

title.description: The player's name for it, or its newest Scene: "Scene 14 · After curfew".

current.description: Whether the player is on it.

played_at.description: When it was last played, ISO 8601; the phone says how long ago.

can_delete.description: False for the Path the player is on.

TryAnotherWayRequest.description: Try another way from a Reply, or, with from null, start again from the beginning (openspec paths).

from.description: The Reply's entry, or null for the Story's opening.

after.description: The head the phone saw; refused as stale if the Story has moved on.

RewindRequest.description: Rewind the Path the player is on to a Reply; what came after is set aside as a Path of its own.

after.description: The head the phone saw; refused as stale if the Story has moved on.

name.description: The Path's new name; empty to go back to its newest Scene.

EditRequest.description: Edit a Move or a Reply in the player's words (openspec scenes: Editing). The latest changes in place; anything earlier carries the Story on from the edit on a new Path.

entry.description: The Move's or the Reply's entry, or a Scene's opening prose.

after.description: The head the phone saw; refused as stale if the Story has moved on.

JournalView.description: The Journal (openspec outside-the-scene: The Journal reads the Story back): the Scenes on the current Path by day, and what the Player Character heard Meanwhile between them, in order.

label.description: "Scene 12 · 6:10 pm · The Three Broomsticks", or with "now" for the Scene the player is in.

summary.description: The Chronicler's line, or empty until it has written one.

now.description: Whether it is the Scene the player is in.

BackstageView.description: Backstage (openspec outside-the-scene: Backstage shows everything else, only when visited): what the Player Character does not know.

offscreen.description: What happened off-screen, by day, newest first, the last seven days.

writer.description: The Writer's plan for the Scene the player is in; null between Scenes.

director.description: What the Director is building toward; null until the Director has planned on this Path.

record.description: The record: each Scene not yet recorded, and each recorded with parts left out, newest first; empty when nothing is missing.

call.description: What the Writer says the next Reply does with the Scene, or null before its first plan.

SceneCall.description: Go on, bring the Scene to its turn, or close it.

BeatStatus.description: Where a beat stands: to come, under way, done, or passed over.

RemoveTasteRequest.description: Delete a lesson from Taste on the Path the player is on (openspec long-run: Taste is short, readable and the player's).

line.description: The lesson to delete, as Taste reads it.

after.description: The head the phone saw; refused as stale if the Story has moved on.
The head the phone saw; refused as stale if the Story has moved on.

on.description: The person to focus on, by name, or null to clear Focus.

RedoRequest.description: Write the latest Reply again. The Direction reaches the Writer only, never the Story.

after.description: The head the phone saw: the latest Reply, or the end of the Scene that Reply closed.

remember.description: Keep the Direction as a line of Taste.

model.description: The model for just this Reply; null or absent for the Story's Actor.

Accepted.description: A change to the Story that is done when it is answered.

PastScene.description: An earlier Scene on the current Path, in full, for reading back (openspec scenes: Scrolling back).

at_label.description: When the Scene began, as people say it.

summary.description: The Chronicler's one line, or empty until it has written one.

ModelProvider.description: Who offers a model: each is reached through the player's own subscription (docs/adr/0005).

ModelChoice.description: Which model does a job: the provider, the id it lists the model under, and the effort when the model has one.

ChosenModel.description: A model as the Models screen shows it: the choice, and its name with the effort ("GPT 6.1 Sol · high").

StoryActor.description: One Story's Actor on the Models screen.

own.description: Set by the player for this Story; otherwise the one its Story File names.

JobModel.description: One job on the Models screen, for every Story.

does.description: What the job does, in one line: "Plans each Reply before it starts".

backup.description: The job's second model, tried once when its own fails or runs too long.

name.description: As the phone shows it: "GPT 6.1 Sol".

efforts.description: The efforts it supports, lowest first; empty when it has none.

ProviderModels.description: What one provider offers, as last asked.

reachable.description: Whether the provider answered the last time it was asked.

reason.description: When not reachable: why, in words the player can read.

models.description: What it offers; when not reachable, what it last offered.

ModelsView.description: The Models screen (openspec outside-the-scene: One Models screen).

actor_backup.description: The Actor's second model, for every Story, tried once before any word of a Reply is written.

SetJobModelRequest.description: Sets the model for a job, from its next work.

backup.description: Sets the job's second model instead of its own.

SetActorRequest.description: Sets a Story's own Actor; null goes back to the one its Story File names.

DirectorPhase.description: Where a stretch of the Story is: building, at its peak, or resting after one.

SceneRef.description: A Scene by its number and title.

CalendarItem.description: A Landmark, or a Happening he knows of, still ahead.

voice.description: Lines they have said, in their own words.

landmarks.description: In the order of their times.

label.description: Where and when: "On screen · Charms, Monday", "Off-screen, Sunday · he heard it from Neville Longbottom", "Off-screen · still to come".
